title: Modular ingest-plugin runtime with tenant-aware sampling and blackhole-safe fallback
creator: Anika Patel
description: Goal: replace the monolithic event intake handler with a lightweight, extensible ingest-plugin runtime that validates, normalizes, and enriches usage events. The runtime must support tenant-aware adaptive sampling policies, a configurable pipeline of transformation plugins, and a robust fallback that safely blackholes or queues malformed events without blocking healthy traffic. This reduces end-to-end latency spikes during schema churn and protects SLOs while preserving actionable telemetry for critical customers.
background: Recent spikes in console metrics correlate with schema drift from third-party SDKs and large batched clients. Current pipeline retries and runtime schema coercion create tail-latency and amplify downstream backpressure. Existing validator services are tightly coupled to the ingestion router which prevents fast canaries and independent scaling. This ticket scopes a modular runtime that can host per-tenant plugin chains (validate, coerce, enrich, audit) and a runtime policy engine for sampling and error handling.
acceptance_criteria: New ingest-plugin runtime deployed behind feature flag on staging
Can attach 3 example plugins: JSON shape validator, tenant-enricher (adds tenant metadata), telemetry-sampler (rules by tenant)
Malformed events: when "drop_on_invalid" policy enabled, pipeline drops and records a minimal summary metric and moves on without increasing request latency beyond 95th percentile baseline
Fail-open behaviour: when plugin runtime crashes or is overloaded, router falls back to lightweight passthrough that tags events as unvalidated and increments fallback metric
End-to-end latency for validated events <= current baseline + 15ms p95 under synthetic load
Integration tests verifying that a schema-change from SDK v1 -> v2 triggers a sampling increase for affected tenants without blocking other tenants
implementation_notes: Prototype implemented in Go as a thin runtime with a plugin registry and protocol based on protobuf envelopes. Plugins run as sandboxed goroutines with a short-circuit API (accept|transform|reject). For safety, plugin execution is limited by CPU/time budgets and circuit-breakers. We will reuse the existing router TLS/auth layer; the runtime exposes a gRPC admin channel for live policy updates. First rollout path is canary on low-volume region and a single test tenant.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: plugin bug could cause silent data loss. Mitigation: build strict telemetry counters, sampling of full raw payloads to a quarantine topic, and a debug mode that mirrors events to a parallel validation stream. Risk: perf regressions. Mitigation: early load tests, perf budget per plugin, and automatic bypass into passthrough mode.
progress_updates: 2025-11-13: spike analysis completed; identified top SDKs causing schema churn
2025-11-15: design review with observability and privacy teams; agreed on minimal quarantine retention (7 days) and secure access patterns
2025-11-18: initial prototype of plugin API merged (PR #4921)
2025-11-20: created integration harness that replays historical traffic to staging cluster for validation
2025-11-24: load test shows plugin runtime adds ~8ms p95 under 1500 rps; tuning ongoing
test_plan: Unit tests for plugin API and policy evaluation. Integration tests that run full plugin chain against synthetic schema-drift inputs. End-to-end replay test comparing metrics between old and new path. Chaos tests to simulate plugin panic and high CPU conditions to validate fallback path.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flagged on staging for 3 days with smoke tests. 2) Canary to region eu-west-1 at 5% traffic for 48h, monitor p95 latency, error budget, and fallback rate. 3) Increase to 25% and run backfill from quarantine for flagged tenants. 4) Full migration and deprecation of monolith router path.
follow_up_tasks: Create RBAC for quarantine access and auditing (PM task)
Add UI in Console to view per-tenant sampling rules and recent quarantined events (Design+PM)
Plan for on-prem variant: limit quarantine retention to customer policy
notes: Avoid schema coercion rules that mutate security-sensitive fields. Coordinate with privacy team for PII redaction plugin before enabling enrichment. Keep plugin API stable-stable contract for 6 months to avoid churn for partners.
